sections.overview: The Annobon White-eye is a small passerine endemic to Annobón, an island of Equatorial Guinea.
sections.identification: It is about 12 cm long, olive-green above, pale below and marked by a narrow white eye-ring.
sections.habitat: It uses primary and secondary woodland, plantations, and even small trees and shrubs in cultivated areas.
sections.diet: It gleans invertebrates from the surfaces of leaves and other vegetation.
sections.behavior: It forages in small parties, typically numbering two to ten birds.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted report a clutch of two eggs but provide little further nesting detail.
sections.ecology: The species is resident and has a very small island range.
sections.conservation: The 2021 global assessment lists it as Least Concern with a stable population trend.
